children: A former chief executive of collapsed tech firm Big Un has been convicted and sentenced for insider trading, Australia's corporate regulator said on Friday, the latest in a series of regulatory actions against the formerly ASX-listed company.

The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) said Richard Evans was sentenced by the District Court of New South Wales to one year and nine months' imprisonment and 400 hours of community service.
As part of the conviction, Evans is disqualified from managing corporations for five years, said ASIC.

Evans, in April, admitted sharing confidential information about a funding arrangement and customer onboarding with a shareholder in January 2017, despite reasonably knowing the shareholder was likely to trade Big Un shares.
At the time, the tech firm was one of the top-performing stocks on the ASX.
Big Un collapsed in 2018 after its shares were suspended from trading and the company later entered administration.
Reuters previously reported the case was a test for Australia's enforcement of market misconduct laws.

ASIC has previously taken action against four people associated with Big Un, including former CFO Andrew Corner, former auditors Graham Rothesay Swan and Jakin Leong Loke and former investment analyst Michael Ming Jinn Ho.
